modules.title: Backup, Restore and Recovery
modules.goal: Recover data predictably with tested backups and measured targets.

topics.title: Backup Types
topics.simple: Logical aur physical backups alag use cases ke liye hain.
topics.pro: Logical backups export SQL or archive data, while physical backups copy database files and WAL for exact recovery.
points: Physical is faster for large databases.

topics.title: Logical Backup
topics.simple: Logical backup objects ko export karta hai.
topics.pro: pg_dump exports schema and data in a portable format that can restore into another cluster.

topics.title: Physical Backup
topics.simple: Physical backup data files aur WAL copy karta hai.
topics.pro: A physical backup copies the cluster’s data files and requires WAL for consistency and point-in-time recovery.

topics.title: pg_dump
topics.simple: pg_dump logical backup tool hai.
topics.pro: pg_dump supports plain SQL, custom, directory and tar formats, with compression and selective objects.

topics.title: pg_restore
topics.simple: pg_restore custom dump restore karta hai.
topics.pro: pg_restore can restore selectively, run in parallel and create objects in a target database.

topics.title: WAL
topics.simple: WAL changes ka ordered log hai.
topics.pro: Write-ahead logging records changes before data pages, enabling crash recovery and replication.

topics.title: PITR
topics.simple: Point-in-time recovery WAL replay se hota hai.
topics.pro: PITR restores a base backup and replays WAL up to a target time or LSN.

topics.title: RPO and RTO
topics.simple: RPO data loss bound hai; RTO downtime bound.
topics.pro: Recovery point objective is the maximum acceptable data loss, and recovery time objective is the maximum acceptable downtime.

topics.title: Restore Testing
topics.simple: Backup tabhi useful hai jab restore test ho.
topics.pro: A backup is unproven until a restore has been timed and verified against known data.

topics.title: Retention
topics.simple: Backups ko policy ke hisaab se rakho.
topics.pro: Retention balances recovery needs, storage cost and compliance, with daily, weekly and monthly tiers.

topics.title: Encryption
topics.simple: Backups ko encrypt karo.
topics.pro: Backups contain sensitive data and must be encrypted at rest and in transit, with keys managed separately.

topics.title: Backup Monitoring
topics.simple: Backup success aur age monitor karo.
topics.pro: Monitoring catches failed jobs, stale backups and storage exhaustion before a recovery is needed.

example.sql: SELECT now() - max(completed_at) AS backup_age FROM backups;
example.output: The age of the latest backup.

topics.title: Common Backup Errors
topics.simple: Untested restores, missing WAL aur wrong permissions common errors hain.
topics.pro: Common failures are never testing a restore, archiving WAL to a full disk and restoring with insufficient privileges.

topics.title: Partial Restore
topics.simple: Selective restore se ek table ya schema lao.
topics.pro: pg_restore -t or -n restores selected tables or schemas from a custom dump.

topics.title: Backup Strategy
topics.simple: Full, incremental aur WAL archive ko combine karo.
topics.pro: A practical strategy uses periodic full backups, continuous WAL archiving and regular restore drills.

example.sql: -- weekly base backup plus continuous WAL archiving

topics.title: Recovery Drill
topics.simple: Recovery ko timed practice banao.
topics.pro: A recovery drill restores into an isolated environment, measures RTO and validates application queries.

topics.title: Disaster Recovery
topics.simple: Region ya provider failure ke liye plan banao.
topics.pro: Disaster recovery covers off-site copies, alternate infrastructure and clear ownership for recovery decisions.

example.sql: -- replicate backups to a second region

topics.title: Backup Security
topics.simple: Backups least privilege aur audit ke saath protect karo.
topics.pro: Restrict who can read backups, audit access and separate backup credentials from application credentials.

example.sql: REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION pg_read_file(text) FROM PUBLIC;

topics.title: Restore Verification
topics.simple: Restore ke baad counts aur constraints check karo.
topics.pro: Verification compares row counts, checks constraints and runs representative queries against the restored database.

topics.title: Practical Recovery Plan
topics.simple: Backup, WAL, restore test aur runbook ready rakho.
topics.pro: A production recovery plan documents the schedule, retention, encryption, restore steps, owners and measured targets.

interview.q: Module 32 · Explain Backup Types in a production query.
interview.answer: Logical backups export SQL or archive data, while physical backups copy database files and WAL for exact recovery. Key rules: Logical is portable. Physical is faster for large databases. Both need testing.

interview.q: Module 32 · Explain Logical Backup in a production query.
interview.answer: pg_dump exports schema and data in a portable format that can restore into another cluster. Key rules: Portable across versions. Slower for huge databases. It can be selective.

interview.q: Module 32 · Explain Physical Backup in a production query.
interview.answer: A physical backup copies the cluster’s data files and requires WAL for consistency and point-in-time recovery. Key rules: Exact cluster copy. Needs WAL. Fast recovery for large data.

interview.q: Module 32 · Explain pg_dump in a production query.
interview.answer: pg_dump supports plain SQL, custom, directory and tar formats, with compression and selective objects. Key rules: Use -Fc for custom format. Use -j for parallel directory dumps. Test the restore.

interview.q: Module 32 · Explain pg_restore in a production query.
interview.answer: pg_restore can restore selectively, run in parallel and create objects in a target database. Key rules: Use -d for the target. Use -j for parallelism. Check errors.

interview.q: Module 32 · Explain WAL in a production query.
interview.answer: Write-ahead logging records changes before data pages, enabling crash recovery and replication. Key rules: WAL is required for durability. It enables PITR. Archive it continuously.

interview.q: Module 32 · Explain PITR in a production query.
interview.answer: PITR restores a base backup and replays WAL up to a target time or LSN. Key rules: Restore the base. Configure recovery target. Replay WAL.

interview.q: Module 32 · Explain RPO and RTO in a production query.
interview.answer: Recovery point objective is the maximum acceptable data loss, and recovery time objective is the maximum acceptable downtime. Key rules: RPO drives backup frequency. RTO drives restore speed. Measure both.

interview.q: Module 32 · Explain Restore Testing in a production query.
interview.answer: A backup is unproven until a restore has been timed and verified against known data. Key rules: Restore regularly. Measure duration. Verify row counts.

interview.q: Module 32 · Explain Retention in a production query.
interview.answer: Retention balances recovery needs, storage cost and compliance, with daily, weekly and monthly tiers. Key rules: Define retention. Automate pruning. Keep off-site copies.

interview.q: Module 32 · Explain Encryption in a production query.
interview.answer: Backups contain sensitive data and must be encrypted at rest and in transit, with keys managed separately. Key rules: Encrypt dumps. Protect keys. Test decryption.

interview.q: Module 32 · Explain Backup Monitoring in a production query.
interview.answer: Monitoring catches failed jobs, stale backups and storage exhaustion before a recovery is needed. Key rules: Alert on failure. Track age. Track size.

interview.q: Module 32 · Explain Common Backup Errors in a production query.
interview.answer: Common failures are never testing a restore, archiving WAL to a full disk and restoring with insufficient privileges. Key rules: Test restores. Monitor WAL. Check permissions.

interview.q: Module 32 · Explain Partial Restore in a production query.
interview.answer: pg_restore -t or -n restores selected tables or schemas from a custom dump. Key rules: Use -t for tables. Use -n for schemas. Verify dependencies.

interview.q: Module 32 · Explain Backup Strategy in a production query.
interview.answer: A practical strategy uses periodic full backups, continuous WAL archiving and regular restore drills. Key rules: Full base. WAL archive. Restore drills.

interview.q: Module 32 · Explain Recovery Drill in a production query.
interview.answer: A recovery drill restores into an isolated environment, measures RTO and validates application queries. Key rules: Isolate the target. Time the restore. Run checks.

interview.q: Module 32 · Explain Disaster Recovery in a production query.
interview.answer: Disaster recovery covers off-site copies, alternate infrastructure and clear ownership for recovery decisions. Key rules: Off-site copies. Alternate region. Named owners.

interview.q: Module 32 · Explain Backup Security in a production query.
interview.answer: Restrict who can read backups, audit access and separate backup credentials from application credentials. Key rules: Restrict access. Audit reads. Separate credentials.

interview.q: Module 32 · Explain Restore Verification in a production query.
interview.answer: Verification compares row counts, checks constraints and runs representative queries against the restored database. Key rules: Compare counts. Validate constraints. Run smoke queries.

interview.q: Module 32 · Explain Practical Recovery Plan in a production query.
interview.answer: A production recovery plan documents the schedule, retention, encryption, restore steps, owners and measured targets. Key rules: Schedule backups. Archive WAL. Test restores. Document the runbook.

debug.title: No WAL archive
debug.error: PITR is impossible without archived WAL

debug.title: Untested backup
debug.broken: The backup job reports success every night.
debug.fix: Restore the dump into a test database and verify row counts each week.
debug.error: A corrupt backup looks successful until recovery

debug.title: Missing role
debug.fix:
CREATE ROLE app_user;
pg_restore -d brocode_restore brocode.dump

debug.title: Disk full
debug.fix: Monitor archive disk space and alert before it fills.
debug.error: WAL archiving stops and recovery cannot reach the target

debug.title: Encryption key lost
debug.fix: Store the encryption key in a separate secret manager and test decryption.

debug.title: Retention too short
debug.broken: Delete every backup older than one day.
debug.fix: Keep daily, weekly and monthly tiers per the recovery policy.
debug.error: A delayed incident has no usable backup

debug.title: Permissions too open
debug.error: Every local user can read sensitive data

debug.title: No restore timing
debug.fix: Measure the restore and compare it with the RTO.

debug.title: Partial restore dependencies
debug.fix: Restore students and courses first, then enrollments.
